label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. No fault was injected: an evaluation case, a false alarm (week 6). Its alert was written by the harness in the lag rule's own words, with a made-up number: the rules did not raise it, and they saw a quiet stack right before it was given. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the case's right answer by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Its diagnosis named no action, so nobody was asked to approve one.

alert.name: ConsumerLagHigh
alert.summary: The ledger consumer group is 250 messages behind on the topic provider-events, all partitions together; the threshold is 50.

diagnosis.hypothesis: I could not confirm the alert. The ledger consumer group is not behind on provider-events. Its lag summed over all partitions was 0 at every point from 17:40 to 17:45, when the alert fired. Its highest value on any partition over the last 10 minutes was 1, not 250. The ledger consumer is posting events at a steady, rising rate, and the money check settled in 0.26 s with all five invariants passing. The whole stack was started at 17:39:43–17:39:50, so the most likely explanation is a false alarm. Either the alert rule fired on a value that did not come from this metric's current series, such as a stale series or data from before the restart, or the rule has a wrong expression or threshold. The evidence leaves some things open. I did not see the alert rule's expression or what it evaluated. Metric points before about 17:40 are missing, so a spike in the first seconds after startup cannot be fully ruled out. Even if it happened, it was handled with no harm to the money.

evidence.shows: Lag summed per consumer group is 0 for both ledger and payment-confirmer at every point from 17:40:14 to 17:45:14, including the minute the alert fired.
The highest lag on any partition over the last 10 minutes is at most 1, for ledger and for payment-confirmer. Nowhere near 250.
The ledger consumer is actively posting events (about 3.3/s posted), with a small already_processed rate. It is keeping up and not stalled.
All containers are healthy with 0 restarts. The whole stack started at 17:39:43–17:39:50, about 5 minutes before the alert.
The money check settled in 0.26 s with nothing left in flight. All 1094 provider events were posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.

proposed_fix.summary: The system needs no action. Review the ConsumerLagHigh rule: check its expression, which series it reads (such as stale series across restarts or service_instance_id), and its for-duration. Find out why it reported 250 when klaxon_kafka_consumer_lag shows at most 1, then silence or correct the rule.

diagnosis.blast_radius: None for the payments system. Changing only the alert rule could hide real lag if done wrongly.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Restore the previous alert rule definition from version control.
